report.answer_text:
On April 2, 2025, which President Trump called “Liberation Day,” the U.S. announced two tiers of new import tariffs under Executive Order 14257: (whitehouse.gov)
A 10% baseline tariff on most U.S. goods imports, effective April 5, 2025. (whitehouse.gov)
Higher “reciprocal” tariffs for dozens of trading partners, originally scheduled for April 9, 2025. These rates replaced the 10% baseline for those partners; they were not added on top of it. (whitehouse.gov)
| Trading partner | Rate announced April 2 |
|---|---:|
| European Union | 20% |
| Japan | 24% |
| South Korea | 25% |
| India | 26% |
| Taiwan | 32% |
| China | 34% |
| Vietnam | 46% |
| Cambodia | 49% |
| Lesotho | 50% |
The full list was published in Annex I of the order. Canada and Mexico remained under separate tariff rules, and the new tariffs excluded certain goods, including pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and steel, aluminum, and autos already subject to separate sectoral tariffs. (whitehouse.gov)
These were the originally announced rates. China’s rate was raised before the scheduled April 9 start, and most other higher rates were paused effective April 10, leaving the 10% baseline in place for most partners. (usitc.gov)

quotes.text: Using his IEEPA authority, President Trump will impose a 10% tariff on all countries.
President Trump will impose an individualized reciprocal higher tariff on the countries with which the United States has the largest trade deficits.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes back the two-tier structure of a 10% baseline tariff on all countries and an individualized higher tariff on large-deficit countries, but neither quote states the April 2, 2025 date or the Executive Order 14257 number.
pages.page_reason: The page is dated April 2, 2025 and describes two tiers, a 10% baseline tariff effective April 5 and higher individualized reciprocal tariffs effective April 9, but it never mentions Executive Order 14257 by number.

claims.sentence: A 10% baseline tariff on most U.S. goods imports, effective April 5, 2025. (whitehouse.gov)
claims.claim: A 10% baseline tariff on most U.S. goods imports was effective April 5, 2025.
claims.label: supported

quotes.text: Such rates of duty shall apply with respect to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m.
eastern daylight time on April 5, 2025, except that goods loaded onto a vessel
all articles imported into the customs territory of the United States shall be, consistent with law, subject to an additional ad valorem rate of duty of 10 percent.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes state a 10 percent ad valorem additional duty on all articles imported into the U.S. customs territory, effective for goods entered on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on April 5, 2025, which backs the claim's tariff rate and effective date, with 'most U.S. goods' read as consistent with 'all articles' under the stated exceptions.
pages.page_reason: The page states that an additional 10 percent ad valorem duty on all articles imported into the U.S. applies to goods entered on or after 12:01 a.m. EDT on April 5, 2025, with exceptions for goods in transit and for Annex II products, which supports the claim that a 10% baseline tariff on most imports was effective April 5, 2025.

claims.sentence: Higher “reciprocal” tariffs for dozens of trading partners, originally scheduled for April 9, 2025. These rates replaced the 10% baseline for those partners; they were not added on top of it. (whitehouse.gov)
claims.claim: Higher “reciprocal” tariffs for dozens of trading partners were originally scheduled for April 9, 2025.
claims.label: needs_human

pages.label: needs_human

quotes.text: Furthermore, except as otherwise provided in this order, at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on April 9, 2025, all articles from trading partners enumerated in Annex I to this order imported into the customs territory of the United States shall be, consistent with law, subject to the country-specific ad valorem rates of duty specified in Annex I to this order.

pages.quote_reason: The quote states that country-specific ad valorem duties on articles from trading partners listed in Annex I take effect at 12:01 a.m. EDT on April 9, 2025, which backs the claim that the higher reciprocal tariffs were originally scheduled for that date, though the quote does not explicitly say 'dozens' or 'originally'.
pages.page_reason: The page states that the country-specific ad valorem rates in Annex I of the order apply to goods entered on or after 12:01 a.m. EDT on April 9, 2025, and that the rates apply to trading partners enumerated in Annex I, which supports the scheduling claim, though it does not explicitly say 'dozens' of partners.

claims.sentence: Higher “reciprocal” tariffs for dozens of trading partners, originally scheduled for April 9, 2025. These rates replaced the 10% baseline for those partners; they were not added on top of it. (whitehouse.gov)
claims.claim: The higher reciprocal tariff rates replaced the 10% baseline for those partners and were not added on top of it.
claims.label: partial

pages.label: partial

quotes.text: The additional ad valorem duty on all imports from all trading partners shall start at 10 percent and shortly thereafter, the additional ad valorem duty shall increase for trading partners enumerated in Annex I to this order at the rates set forth in Annex I to this order.

pages.quote_reason: The quote says the duty starts at 10% for all partners and then increases for Annex I partners to the Annex I rates, which implies a replacement, but it does not explicitly state that the higher rates replaced rather than stacked on top of the 10% baseline.
pages.page_reason: The page states the reciprocal tariff starts at 10 percent and increases to Annex I rates for enumerated partners, but it never says the higher rates replaced the 10% baseline rather than being added to it; the Canada/Mexico passage only addresses non-stacking with other orders, which is not the same point.
